tasks.outcome: Make each built copy of the program carry the version of the code it was built from.
Obtain Microsoft's current set of policy definitions and install them in a folder the program can use.
Be offered the full set of policy definitions the first time the program is used on an edition that lacks them.
Make the newly downloaded policy definitions the ones the program works with.
Get back to the policy work where it was left: the last policy sources and policy definitions are ready to browse.
Choose the language in which policy definition text is shown and have it applied.
Finish the work and leave, releasing everything that was opened.
Find out who made the program and which version is in use.
Decide where the user and computer policies are kept and start working against those sources.
Name the user account whose own Group Policy object is to be the user policy source.
Choose a user profile whose stored settings are to be the user policy source.
Save the policy settings and comments to their sources, make them take effect where possible, and remember the chosen sources for next time.
Set one policy to Enabled, Disabled or Not configured, with its options and comment, for the computer or the user.
Bring a set of policy settings in from a semantic policy text and apply them to the computer and user policy sources.
See policy settings as semantic policy text and copy it out to use elsewhere.
Go straight to a known category, product, support definition or policy by typing its identifier.
Find policies whose title, description or comments contain words or phrases the person remembers.
Find the policies that control a given system setting, named by its key or value.
Work through the hits of a search and pick the policy to open.
Limit the policy list to policies of a chosen type, state, comment status and supported products, and switch that limit on or off.
Open a policy file for direct editing of its raw keys and values, with a warning the first time, and leave the editor when done.
Add a new key, or a new value of a chosen kind, to a policy file.
Change the data of an existing value in a policy file.
Remove keys or values from a policy file, either leaving a deletion instruction for the machine or forgetting them entirely.
Bring the contents of an exported set of machine settings into a policy source.
Load a policy file into the user or computer policy source.
Write a policy source, or one branch of it, as an exported set of machine settings.
Save a policy source out as a policy file.
Load a folder of policy definitions into the workspace so its policies can be browsed.
Add a single policy template file to the policies already loaded.
Remove all loaded policy definitions from the workspace.
See which policy template files are loaded and what each one contributes.
Move through the categories and policies of the loaded definitions and read what each is for.
Merge identical user and computer policies into single policies that apply to both.
See what a policy is, which section it applies to, where it sits and what it is supported on.
See a category, its parent and how it relates to policies.
Browse the products and their versions that the loaded definitions cover, and see the details of each.
Find the support rules and see which products they cover.
Inspect the technical makeup of a policy: its stored setting, presentation, elements and semantic text, and copy it.
